name: KSB Ltd
tagline: Debt-free MNC pump & valve maker (ROCE ~25%) with a genuine nuclear / critical-process order catalyst and a capex-led capacity theme - a high-quality compounder, but at ~Rs 14,000 Cr market cap and ~8x book with single-digit recent growth it is not a 10x/100x open-screen fit
business_overview: KSB Ltd is the listed Indian arm of Germany's KSB SE, making centrifugal pumps, industrial valves and related systems for water/waste-water, power (including nuclear), oil & gas, chemicals, building services and general industry. It runs foundries and machining plants (Pimpri, Chinchwad, Khandala, Coimbatore, Sinnar, Vambori) and has been adding capacity. The trusted-X watch note flags a news snippet: KSB "reports breakthrough and first-ever orders for some critical applications across key sectors" - read as nuclear / critical-process pump and valve wins, aligned with India's nuclear-capacity expansion (700 MWe PHWR fleet, SMR roadmap).
fundamentals_table: ~Rs 13,800-15,200 Cr (upper mid-cap); CMP mid-range, 52-wk Rs 668.6 - Rs 1,028
FY25 revenue ~Rs 2,726 Cr, +6.4% YoY - well below the 5-yr CAGR of ~17.4% (a soft patch, not a collapse)
~8.1x book value; rich - priced as a quality compounder / MNC re-rating candidate
Debtor days up 97 -> 118; MNC parent, periodic management-change / export-mandate optionality
fundamentals_narrative: Quality is genuinely high: ROCE ~25%, ROE ~18%, essentially no debt, an MNC parent, and a multi-year capex/capacity-expansion theme. But FY25 revenue grew only ~6.4% against a ~17% five-year CAGR, debtor days have stretched to 118, and the stock already trades at ~8x book - so the market is paying up-front for a re-acceleration. The nuclear / critical-application order note is a real positive catalyst (India is expanding nuclear capacity and KSB is an established supplier of primary-circuit and safety-class pumps), but a single order-win announcement does not convert a ~Rs 14,000 Cr, single-digit-growth, richly-valued name into a near-term multibagger.
technical_read: Not independently pulled (tier-4.8 watch exit). Trading between the Rs 668.6 - Rs 1,028 52-week band.

bull_case: High-quality franchise: ROCE ~25%, ROE ~18%, debt-free, MNC parent, capacity-expansion theme
Nuclear / critical-process order catalyst aligns with India's nuclear-capacity build-out (700 MWe PHWR fleet, SMR roadmap) - KSB is an established safety-class pump supplier
Optionality from parent export mandates and management change (the classic KSB re-rating thesis)
bear_case: At ~Rs 14,000 Cr market cap, ~8x book, and only ~6% recent revenue growth, a 10x-in-2-3-years outcome is not credible; 100x-in-10-years even less so - realistic base case is a mid-teens compounder, not a multibagger
FY25 growth (~6.4%) well below the 5-year CAGR; debtor days stretched 97 -> 118
Rich valuation already discounts a re-acceleration - limited margin of safety if order inflow stays lumpy
verdict_headline: High-quality debt-free pump/valve MNC with a real nuclear-order catalyst, but too large and too richly valued for the open-screen 10x/100x thesis - trusted-X watch snippet, not a call, exits with a last_analyzed_date
verdict_reasoning: Entered as a trusted-x-watch snippet from @a_basumallick: quote - "Reports breakthrough and first-ever orders for some critical applications across key sectors" (pumps/valves; likely nuclear/critical process) (news snippet, 2026-08-18). This was a news mention with no stated view, not a conviction call.
No red flag: ROCE ~25%, ROE ~18%, debt-free, MNC parent - clears the quality gate.

Size math: at ~Rs 14,000 Cr market cap with ~Rs 2,726 Cr revenue growing ~6.4%, a literal 10x in 2-3 years or 100x in 10 years is not defensible. The trailing-average-vs-live-inflection rule does not rescue the label here - the recent quarter is soft (not a strong specific inflection), the catalyst (one order announcement) is unconfirmed in scale, and the stock is already priced at ~8x book. thesis_fit 'neither'.

The large-cap inflection exception does not apply: capex-led capacity addition and a nuclear order win are ordinary industrial-cycle progression, not a specific named management or industry-structure regime change.

No live-theme match drove entry (watch-tier snippet); the nuclear-order angle touches the priority-2 'uranium / nuclear fuel / SMR / nuclear power' theme, worth noting if a future run re-promotes it as a focused nuclear-capex proxy.
Conviction Low, revisit_after_30d false. Exits here as a snippet watch; re-promote only if a specific, sized order pipeline or a structural inflection emerges.
